::: {.callout-tip title="Using this template" icon=false}
Describe how the dataset was produced so that another person can understand,
check and repeat the work. Replace the bracketed prompts with your own text.
Keep these instructional notes while developing the report and remove them
when it is complete. Add rows and repeat method sections wherever needed.
:::

Word users: save a project copy as `data_dev_project.docx`.
Type directly into it and use the existing heading styles when adding sections.
The report records methods and lineage; `metadata.pdf` describes the dataset
for users and `citation.txt` provides its saved citation.

# Project summary

## Purpose

::: {.callout-tip title="What to write" icon=false}
Explain why the dataset is needed, who will use it and which question or
decision it supports. State the intended geographic and temporal coverage.
:::

[Write the purpose and intended use here.]

## Scope and key definitions

[Describe what the work includes and excludes. Define specialist terms and
any boundaries, scales or assumptions needed to understand the methods.]

# Main steps

::: {.callout-tip title="What to write" icon=false}
Summarise the workflow in order. Give each step a stable identifier that can
also be used in the detailed methods, scripts, logs and validation records.
:::

| Step | Main activity | Result |
|:-----|:--------------|:-------|
| S01 | [Prepare and check inputs] | [Prepared inputs] |
| S02 | [Process or derive data] | [Derived outputs] |
| S03 | [Validate and assemble products] | [Checked products] |

# Datasets used

::: {.callout-tip title="What to record" icon=false}

manifest. Note any restrictions, selection, exclusions or preprocessing.
:::

| Input | Citation and version | Location and role |
|:------|:---------------------|:------------------|
| I01 [Title] | [Citation; version/date; identifier] | [Relative path or stable URL; use] |
| I02 [Title] | [Citation; version/date; identifier] | [Relative path or stable URL; use] |

**Input selection and preparation:** [Explain inclusion rules, exclusions,
permissions relevant to reuse and any preparation completed before S01.]

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Data processing

::: {.callout-tip title="What to write" icon=false}
Repeat the method section below for each main step. Describe what was actually
done, why it was done that way and the settings that affect the result.
Manual work in QGIS, ArcGIS, spreadsheets or field records is equally valid:
record selections, tools, settings and decisions even when there is no code.
:::

## S01 Step title

**Objective and rationale**

[Explain what this step achieves and why this approach was selected.]

**Inputs and prerequisites**

[Identify input IDs, versions, layers or sheets, and any preceding steps.]

**Method**

[Describe the operations in sufficient detail for another practitioner to
repeat them. Include formulas, diagrams or screenshots where they clarify
the method. Cite published methods and explain any departures from them.]

**Parameters and decision rules**

| Setting | Value and units | Reason or source |
|:--------|:----------------|:-----------------|
| [Parameter or rule] | [Actual value] | [Rationale or citation] |
| [Parameter or rule] | [Actual value] | [Rationale or citation] |

**Implementation and execution evidence**

[Record software and tool names; script or model path and code revision if
applicable; run ID and date; and relative paths to logs or saved commands.
Refer to Appendix D for the full processing environment.]

**Outputs and checks**

[Identify outputs from this step, checks performed, results and any failures,
corrections or exceptions. Distinguish a completed check from a planned check.]

**Decisions and limitations**

[Explain judgement calls, rejected alternatives, uncertainty and limitations
introduced by this step. Refer to decision IDs in Appendix E where useful.]

|:--------------------------|:--------------------------|:------------|

**Packaging and completeness:** [State what is included, what is excluded,
how NoData or missing values are represented and where the file manifest or
checksum record is stored.]

## Quality assessment

::: {.callout-tip title="What to write" icon=false}
Report the checks and their evidence. Include relevant completeness, spatial,
attribute, numerical or independent-review checks. Record unresolved issues
as well as successful results; do not describe an untested result as passed.
:::

| Check and acceptance criterion | Result | Evidence |
|:-------------------------------|:-------|:---------|
| [Check; expected outcome] | [Measured result; status] | [Log, table or review path] |
| [Check; expected outcome] | [Measured result; status] | [Log, table or review path] |

**Known limitations and appropriate use:** [Explain uncertainty, unsuitable
applications and any conditions a downstream user must consider.]

# Conclusion

[Explain whether the purpose was achieved, which products are ready for use,
what remains unresolved and which further work is recommended.]
